title: Sheet Pan Tandoori Chicken (Keto, Whole30)
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot), grams derived FROM the printed measure via db\densities.json (or the flagged label/USDA unit weights where densities has no row) so the two agree by construction; quantities quantized to house quarters, drift from the exact 3.5x scale noted per line where it exceeds 5%. Marinade counted in full, matching the source's own nutrition basis.
ruled_substitutions: Avocado oil -> Olive Oil, SOURCE-SANCTIONED: the line itself prints '1 tablespoon avocado oil or fat of choice'. The avocado-oil commodity exists but is CAPTURE-tier (no priced board cell today, 25 capture candidates); olive-oil is priced 7 of 7 and is a sanctioned 'fat of choice'. Fat macros are within 1 cal/tbsp. This avoids parking the recipe on a 1-tbsp pan-greasing line the source itself makes fungible.
Coconut milk line offers 'or plain coconut yogurt'; the PRIMARY (full-fat canned coconut milk) is booked, matching the recipe's Whole30 framing and the source's nutrition basis.

registrar_rulings.status: PENDING - proposal drafted, registrar not yet consulted (mapper lane cannot invoke the registrar agent; orchestrator must route it)
registrar_rulings.mapper_sweep_evidence: price-ingredient.ps1 verdict ABSENT for both 'tandoori spice mix' and 'tandoori seasoning' ('no board cell and nothing in any capture matches'). No tandoori id in commodities.json or recipe-commodities.json. NOT mapped to any existing spice commodity: tandoori masala is a distinct multi-spice blend product (a curry-powder-class shelf item, not paprika or garam masala re-labeled); nearest-neighbor spice mapping is the variety-pricing rejection class. Shan/Rani/McCormick tandoori blends are standard international-aisle items at Walmart/Hy-Vee class stores, so carriage is plausible; the pricer rules.
registrar_rulings.meanwhile: ingredient maps item_id null (safe pantry-static pricing); term 'tandoori spice mix' enqueued BLOCKING - it is the marinade's identity and the dish's name.

macro_cross_check.verdict: Protein PASS at +13.3% (inside the 15% instrument, direction consistent with our raw-weight basis) - the main protein is an explicit source weight (1.5 lb), so portions stand. The -32% calorie gap is FAT-shaped (theirs 45 g vs ours 21.6 g) and back-computes cleanly to one explanation: their calculator booked SKIN-ON thigh macros (~2.2 cal/g raw; 1.5 lb skin-on = ~1,500 cal vs our 850 from the label-accurate boneless-skinless row - a ~163 cal/serving gap, plus their avocado-oil entry) while the printed ingredient is 'boneless and skinless'. Booking skin-on macros against a skinless ingredient would be the false claim; our row matches the printed food.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 401.2 cal PASSES the [400, 650] floor BY 1.2 CAL - razor thin and called out loudly. Sensitivity, honestly stated: (a) cauliflower heads booked at 540 g florets each (the ~2 lb-head yield the source's own bound implies); genuinely smaller 'small' heads at ~450 g compute 393.2 and FAIL; (b) the Shan tandoori row at 25 cal/tbsp contributes 12.5 cal/serving - a lighter blend basis (some labels print ~10 cal/tsp on 2 g teaspoons) moves the serving about -2 to +6 cal. The honest range straddles the floor, so the auditor should treat this as AT-FLOOR pending the pricer's tandoori verdict and any head-weight ruling; do not adjust numbers to fit. Carbs 11.1 g <= 35 PASS with room throughout the range. Optional lines excluded (cilantro + lemon add ~2.6 cal/serving if counted - which would coincidentally clear the floor, and is exactly the kind of convenient counting this gate exists to refuse).

loud_flags: AT-FLOOR: 401.2 cal vs the 400 floor, inside any honest error bar (cauliflower head weight, tandoori blend basis). Auditor should rule with eyes open rather than trust the fourth significant figure.
Recipe PARKS in 'pricing' on one term (tandoori spice mix) that is also a pending registrar proposal - the dish cannot honestly ship without a tandoori price, it is the name of the recipe.
Source's published fat (45 g) matches skin-on thighs while its printed ingredient says skinless - their label, not ours, carries the internal contradiction; documented in the cross-check.
board_defects_observed: Term resolver misfire: bare 'coconut milk' answers via the DAIRY milk commodity (/\bmilk\b/ include) at $/gallon - a canned pantry item priced as fresh dairy; 'canned coconut milk' resolves correctly to coconut-milk-canned. Queue/spec phrasing must use the qualified term.

avocado-oil commodity exists with NO priced board cell (CAPTURE, 25 candidates across 2 stores) - a real gap for the growing share of recipes that name avocado oil; flagged for the pricer/match-soundness gate, not exercised here thanks to the source's 'fat of choice' sanction.
densities_followups: Cauliflower: STILL no densities row (fourth recipe in this run to need one); proposed cup 107 / head ~540 medium stands, and a 'small' key would have decided this recipe's floor question cleanly.
Tandoori Masala: no densities row; propose tbsp 8 / tsp 2.7 (Shan USDA-branded basis).
Kosher salt: densities Salt row is fine-salt basis (6 g/tsp); a kosher_tsp ~3 g key would remove the manual halving every Diamond-Crystal line requires.
